questions.question: What is the central release invariant for a progressive deployment?
options: Increase traffic on a fixed schedule until it reaches 100%
Keep a known-good path while the new version is observable, compatible, and reversible
Deploy every database change with the application binary
Use the same strategy for every service
questions.explanation: A progressive rollout needs bounded exposure, evidence, compatibility, and a route back before it can safely expand.

questions.question: Which constraint most strongly favors blue-green deployment?
options: The service has no spare capacity for any additional instances
A planned maintenance window permits downtime
Traffic must return to a complete prior environment very quickly
The team has no traffic-routing control
questions.explanation: Blue-green keeps a standby environment so ingress can switch back quickly, at the cost of duplicate runtime capacity and data-migration discipline.

questions.question: Why does a rolling update require compatibility between old and new versions?
options: Both versions serve traffic during instance replacement
It always duplicates the entire environment
It prevents any traffic from reaching the old version
It automatically reverses database schema changes
questions.explanation: A rolling update creates a mixed fleet for part of the release, so contracts, state, and schema behavior must work for both versions.

questions.question: What distinguishes shadow traffic from a canary?
options: Shadow traffic always writes to the production database
A canary receives no real requests
Shadow traffic keeps the stable response for customers while the candidate is evaluated separately
A canary can never be rolled back
questions.explanation: Shadowing is a comparison technique. The stable path remains customer-facing while eligible requests are safely mirrored to the candidate.

questions.question: A 10% canary breaches its error and checkout-success guardrails. What should happen first?
options: Raise the canary to 25% to collect more data
Freeze promotion and route new requests back to the stable version
Delete the candidate database columns
Wait for the next scheduled deployment
questions.explanation: The immediate objective is to stop additional customer exposure. Diagnosis and any data repair follow after routing has restored the stable path.

questions.question: Why is an expand-migrate-contract database change safer than a direct destructive schema change?
options: It removes the need for rollback planning
It lets old and new application versions coexist while data moves in bounded steps
It guarantees the migration has no operational cost
It requires all clients to update at exactly the same time
questions.explanation: Adding compatible structures first, migrating while both versions work, and removing old structures only after retirement preserves the rollback window.
